rationale:
Evidence from iteration 8 (score 218.1, best so far). Widening the sensor row from ±0.06 m to ±0.08 m fixed slalom line loss (0.9 events down to 0) and raised oval completions to 9 of 20, with oval oscillation down to 0.20. But s-bend progress fell from 0.30 to 0.11, and slalom progress stayed at about 0.08. Every track still ends at max_error of about 0.06 m, the off-track limit, so the robot overshoots on bends rather than losing the line.

The wider row also lowers the steering signal per unit of lateral offset. The weights run from -1 to +1 over ±0.08 m, a slope of 12.5 per metre, versus 16.7 per metre at ±0.06 m. That is about 25 percent less effective steering gain, which fits the s-bend collapse and the stalled slalom. Iteration 8 H1 predicted this: the excursion is steering lag, not sensor coverage.

Change: kp 4.5 to 5.0, the only change. This restores about 11 percent of the lost steering authority while keeping the ±0.08 m coverage that fixed line loss. kd stays at 0.9 and oscillation has margin (0.20 on oval). The wider row, weights, wheel_track, mass and base_speed are unchanged so the effect of gain can be read cleanly.

Expected result: s-bend progress back toward 0.2 or more, slalom progress above 0.1, oval completions holding at 8 or more, and oval steering_oscillation below about 0.3. Hypotheses: (H1) if oval oscillation rises above 0.35, kp is too high for kd, so kd should drop to 0.7. (H2) if s-bend and slalom still stall near 0.1 progress with max_error at 0.06, the limit is speed on the tighter bends, so base_speed should drop to about 1.0. (H3) if all tracks survive but do not finish, base_speed should rise to about 1.2. Measurements wanted per track: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort and noise_robustness.
